newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss shares give up most gains, end slightly up.
newsitem.headline: Swiss shares give up most gains, end slightly up.

text.p: 1540 GMT - Swiss shares ended just a shade above Wednesday's close after a slide following new all-time highs reached in early trading.
Dealers said profit-taking after an enthusiastic start marred sentiment. Also, derivatives-related selling pressured the market.
The blue-chip SMI index may move in a range between 3,900 and 3,930 points on Friday if "there is no pressure from Wall Street", one dealer noted.
* The SMI ended up 3.2 points, or 0.08 percent, at 3,913.8.
* The all-share SPI added 2.46 points to 2,498.06.
The SMI reached an all-time high at 3,937.5 points.

Most-active Roche certificates added 30 francs to 10,160. Investment Trust Pharma Vision had no comment on rumours that it had sold Roche stock. Speculation swirled in Stockholm that a big Roche shareholder had swapped out shares for those in Sweden's Astra. Astra denied rumours that Roche management was in Stockholm to meet Astra today.
Swiss dealers said it was improbable that Roche would plan to take over Astra. Roche is often mentioned as a possible suitor when speculation focuses on a large pharmaceutical group.
Ciba and Sandoz firmed around 0.4 percent each.
* Surveillance shares jumped nearly two percent to 3,145. Dealers said the stocks surged after a major bank recommended the shares.

* Banks were generally lower. CS Holding slumped 1.1 percent to 135 francs. UBS bearer shares and SBC slid 0.4 percent each to 1,207 francs and 253.75 francs, respectively. Insurers generally firmed. Baloise shot up 3.3 percent to 2,960 francs.
* On the Swiss Options and Futures Exchanged (Soffex), trade concentrated on SMI options.

The SMI options trading volume reached 109,768 contracts, which amounted to 67 percent of the total of 163,245 options contracts, dealers said. Options on Nestle and on major pharmaceuticals were also in demand.
On the futures side, 4,131 SMI contracts changed hands.
